title: Confiscation of vehicle in excise cases - how to get it released
p1: Your vehicle can be seized in an excise case even if you are not the person who committed the alleged offence. Many owners are surprised to learn that simply proving ownership may not be enough to get the vehicle back immediately.
p2: A common misconception is that once police seize a vehicle, the owner has no option until the criminal case ends. In reality, excise laws often provide a separate process where the owner can approach the appropriate authority for release of the vehicle, subject to legal conditions.
p3: The key is acting quickly. A release application usually requires showing valid ownership, explaining the circumstances, and assuring that the vehicle will be produced when required. In many cases, delay can lead to unnecessary loss of time and value of the vehicle. A seizure does not always mean permanent loss.
